prompt: A wide, split-panel illustration showing a colossal, translucent cube made of countless tiny glowing numbers hovering in the center, like a three-dimensional spreadsheet. From the left, a tall corporate tower with locked doors and a toll booth extends a tethered cable toward the cube, with users lining up to access it through a guarded terminal. From the right, the cube's numerical contents pour downward like a waterfall of digits into an open shipping crate beside an ordinary person's home workstation, where the same cube — an identical copy — floats above a personal computer, complete and unbound. Inside the home scene, small details carry the entry's tensions: a robust-looking GPU rack hinting at the hardware needed to run the copy; a hand reaching into the cube to pluck out and rearrange digits, showing it can be modified; a padlock icon visibly detaching from the copied cube, signaling that built-in safeguards can be stripped away; and behind everything, a stylized one-way turnstile door through which the numbers have passed and can never return, rendered in bold red as the image's focal warning. A caption-like banner across the bottom distinguishes the two halves: on the tower side, "closed: rules and prices"; on the home side, "open weights: download, run, change — no going back."
